headline: 154 Million Lives Saved: The Quiet Power of Vaccines
meta_description: Since 1974, vaccination has averted 154 million deaths and gained 10.2 billion years of full health globally.
summary_short: Vaccines have averted 154 million deaths since 1974—including 146 million children under 5. For every life saved, 66 years of healthy life were gained.
body:
Since 1974, vaccination has averted 154 million deaths worldwide. Among these, 146 million were children younger than 5 years old, and 101 million were infants younger than 1 year. The human cost of this prevention is staggering in reverse: for every death averted, an average of 66 years of full health were gained—totaling 10.2 billion years of healthy life across the globe.

The impact has been most profound where it matters most. Vaccination accounts for 40 percent of the observed decline in global infant mortality, but in the African region, that figure rises to 52 percent—meaning more than half of Africa's infant mortality reduction is directly attributable to immunization programs.

These numbers reflect decades of quiet, systematic progress: millions of needles administered, countless clinics staffed, supply chains maintained across continents. Each statistic represents a child who survived, a parent who didn't lose a son or daughter, a community that remained intact. Vaccination remains one of public health's most cost-effective interventions.
quick_facts: 146 million were children under 5 years old
101 million were infants younger than 1 year
10.2 billion years of full health gained globally
52% of African infant mortality decline due to vaccines
